en: The ritual of bathing for the purpose of purifying oneself is taught here;

it is praised according to worldly custom because of its prescription for the rules of purity and conduct. That ritual action of bathing is now explained in detail through its various classifications.
With the self-nature of the armor and the yoga of the wrathful one, [one should visualize] the ten directions starting from the three syllables.
For the sake of abandoning all misfortunes, one should manifest Vajrayakṣa;
indeed, one should manifest oneself as the wrathful Vighnāntaka in the form of a wrathful deity.
Oṃ kili 2 vajra hūṃ phaṭ.
One should consecrate [it] with this mantra. Oṃ ṭuḥ kavacaḥ hūṃ.
Oṃ hūṃ vajrayakṣa!
Oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali phaṭ! Amṛtakuṇḍaleḥ!
One should visualize oneself as the terrible one, difficult to endure due to vajra-flames,
by means of this vajra-mantra and the vajra-flame mudrā:
*oṃ dhupi dhupi kāyadhupini svāhā*.
For the purpose of bringing forth the fruit, one should cast three handfuls of water while reciting this mantra: "O Great One who possesses fangs and inspires fear!
Whatever belongs to the entire Buddha-family and whatever knowledge is desired—
Having empowered three clay figurines with the mantra,
the wise practitioner should smear their bodies with those mudrās— namely, the upper, lower, and middle parts—
with the right hand on the left [figurine] and the left hand on the right.
And that, moreover, is performed through the application of gesture (abhinaya) in the sequence beginning with the upward direction.
Its mantra is: Oṃ jvale svāhā.
By the upward casting of water with all the mudrās, all obstacles are summoned;
having recollected all the Buddhas, this is considered the secret mantra through the vidyā.
By this very [mantra], one performs the binding of the directions, beginning with Śakra in the eastern quarter.
King Yama shall be in the south, and Varuṇa in the west;
Dhanada likewise in the north—these four figures are made of clay.
Having taken the crow from the directions, two figures are placed in the upper half.
Having likewise performed this in the intermediate directions, the binding of obstacles will be accomplished.
With the blazing Vajramuṣṭi and the Vajralocana mudrā,
and with the Vajra-flame Fire-Sun, the binding of obstacles will be accomplished.
Then, having bathed and performed prostrations in the four directions by the high-souled ones,
one should form the eight seats through the yoga of the four seals in the four directions;
the fifth belongs to Akṣobhya and consists of the clenched fist at the waist.

Then, by wandering precisely through the intermediate directions, the highly fortunate Vajrācārya should perform the hymn of praise and the names— the supreme and most excellent secret. Having performed this without obstruction, he should then produce the threefold worship.
But worship must indeed be performed through practice by the most excellent noble beings. Furthermore, you are asked here: how should the fire offering (*homa*) be performed?
Bodily action is threefold, while verbal action is fourfold. [8.15–8.16]
One should indeed perform the supreme mental homa in three ways; by means of such a procedure, one becomes composed of all merit. [8.17] The Ritual of Bathing.
